newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Barak on surprise visit to Amman.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Barak on surprise visit to Amman.

text.p: Israeli opposition leader Ehud Barak flew to Amman on Monday on a surprise visit at the invitation of Jordan's King Hussein, officials said.
"He is on the way there. He got an unexpected invitation from King Hussein," said an official in Barak's Labour party, declining to offer further details.
In Tel Aviv, a Jordanian embassy official said the king had sent a plane to pick up Barak, a former army chief who last month succeeded ousted Prime Minister Shimon Peres as Labour party leader.
Jordan has been looking for ways to break a four-month-old deadlock in Israeli-Palestinian peace talks prompted by the building of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
In PLO-ruled Ramallah on Sunday, Jordan's Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali met Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat to review ways of breaking the impasse.
"We will use all means available to us to support the Palestinians. If we are asked to help, we will always be there." Majali said on Sunday.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who has angered the king by his right-wing policies on Jerusalem and Jewish settlements, resists the peace deals signed by Barak's Labour party based on the principle of land-for-peace.
